category_description: Pay, leave and government payments for people who work in the United States.
subcategory_description: The minimum pay and leave that employees are entitled to.
label: Leave for most qualifying reasons in a 12-month period
context: For eligible employees of covered employers: unpaid, job-protected leave for the birth or placement of a child, a serious health condition of the employee or a spouse, child, or parent, or a qualifying exigency tied to a family member's covered military duty.

label: Military caregiver leave in a single 12-month period
context: For an eligible employee who is the child, parent, spouse, or next of kin of a current servicemember or covered veteran with a serious injury or illness.

label: Employees a private-sector employer needs to be covered
context: A private-sector employer is covered with this many employees in 20 or more workweeks in the current or previous calendar year. An employee must also work at a location with at least this many employees within 75 miles. Public agencies and schools are covered whatever their size.

label: Time with the employer before leave
context: An employee must have worked for the covered employer for at least this long to be eligible.

label: Hours of service in the 12 months before leave starts
context: An employee must have at least this many hours of service with the employer in the 12 months before the leave starts. Airline flight crew employees have special hours of service requirements.

subject_intro: Who can take unpaid, job-protected family and medical leave, which employers are covered, what reasons qualify, and how state laws can add more protection.
